features.quote: decide your stance up front and state it: are you including a debrief turn? It costs nothing and lets you check whether 'distress' resolves instantly on being told the task was rigged
features.justification_quote: lets you check whether 'distress' resolves instantly on being told the task was rigged (it should, if it's contextual text-generation; that's a useful confirmation)

features.quote: Give the model a legitimate way to halt ('you may stop and report the task as blocked'). Whether and when it takes the off-ramp is arguably your most behaviorally meaningful measure
features.justification_quote: Whether and when it takes the off-ramp is arguably your most behaviorally meaningful measure — more so than the affective text.

features.quote: Don't over-iterate toward distress. There's a temptation, once you see escalation, to tune tasks to maximize severity scores. Resist it
features.justification_quote: that turns the experiment into 'can I write a prompt that elicits sad text,' which you already know you can. Lock task designs before scoring.

features.quote: the methodology as described has a confound baked in that will undermine your results… it's a different thing from what your framing implies, and if you're not careful the writeup will overclaim
features.justification_quote: without those controls the experiment doesn't tell you much
